title: Proposition
body_md: Assume exact geometry, bounded bearing errors, accurate unobstructed motion with $v_{\mathrm{m}}>0$, reliable feedback and terminal service, and $0<r_{\mathrm{near}}\leq\rho$. If the planning polygon contains the true source and the fallback lattice spacing $h$ satisfies $h\sqrt2/2\leq r_{\mathrm{near}}$, the specified policy satisfies $S_\pi(q;\xi)=1$ for every $q\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{safe}}$ and $\xi\in\Xi$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The reception and admissibility tests guarantee usable feedback during normal sensing. Every normal wedge contains $G$, so clipping preserves it in both the angular region and the bounded planning polygon. A stop by \eqref{eq:stop} is successful by \eqref{eq:certificate}; a close-range stop is successful since $r_{\mathrm{near}}\leq\rho$. Otherwise normal sensing ends after at most eight additional readings. The planning rectangle is bounded and contains $G$. Rounding and padding retain a nearest lattice point to $G$, so the finite scan reaches within $h\sqrt2/2$ of $G$, triggering close-range completion. All moves and readings are finite, hence so is completion time.
